seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: compared with unstructured selection, proposals touching more sampled witnesses and witness-load mass, reconnecting more remotely, and creating fewer local risks will more often reduce the next authoritative forbidden-cycle penalty; this can be falsified by matched-pool follow-up reductions.
assumptions: More sampled witnesses touched predicts greater true forbidden-cycle reduction.
Greater removed-edge witness-load mass predicts a more useful rewrite.
Greater reconnection distance predicts lower newly created forbidden-cycle risk.
Greater combined local triangle and 4-cycle risk predicts a worse rewrite.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: compared with unstructured selection, this lexicographically prioritizes lower bounded local triangle/C4 risk, then favors larger bounded sampled-witness coverage and edge-load proxies, which should more often select early moves associated with fewer later forbidden-cycle witnesses; this is falsifiable by comparing subsequent authoritative scores across selected moves.
assumptions: Lower combined local triangle and C4 risk is associated with lower downstream forbidden-cycle risk, but local counts may be partial and provide no guarantee.
More sampled witnesses broken is associated with greater forbidden-cycle reduction.
Higher removed-edge sampled witness load is associated with greater forbidden-cycle reduction; this proxy may be redundant or misleading.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: weighting proposal-specific sampled witness hits and edge loads by current forbidden-cycle counts, while penalizing local risks and piecewise-adjusting exploration from stagnation or remaining_steps, will select mutations that reduce forbidden-cycle witnesses earlier than an unstructured rule; this is falsified if it does not improve early accepted reductions under identical proposal pools.
assumptions: Larger current capped cycle counts identify more valuable forbidden lengths, despite being capped and not guaranteed to predict improvement.
Larger broken sampled witness counts and removed-edge witness loads predict greater reduction of forbidden-cycle witnesses.
Greater separation among removed edges and greater remoteness of newly connected endpoints are beneficial heuristics.
Larger local triangle and C4 risk predicts a worse rewrite.
Stagnation or a short remaining horizon warrants more exploitation of witness-breaking and risk-avoiding signals than broad structural exploration.
Bounded sampled witnesses and local-risk counts are sufficiently informative proxies for the authoritative post-rewrite score.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: equal-weight averages of aligned per-length witness-hit and witness-load fractions, combined with graph-order-normalized removed-edge separation, will select mutations that reduce forbidden-cycle witnesses earlier than unstructured selection; this is falsified if these priorities do not yield lower authoritative forbidden-cycle penalties along otherwise comparable search trajectories.
assumptions: A larger per-length sampled-witness hit fraction tends to indicate a better rewrite.
A larger per-length sampled witness-load fraction tends to indicate a better rewrite.
Greater normalized separation between removed edges tends to indicate a better rewrite.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: prioritizing proposals that touch more sampled forbidden witnesses and higher-load witness edges should beat unstructured selection, while a small k bonus should help larger switches only when their bounded local triangle/C4 risk is controlled.
assumptions: More broken sampled witnesses indicate greater expected reduction of forbidden-cycle witnesses.
Higher removed-edge sampled witness load indicates greater expected usefulness.
Higher current capped witness counts identify cycle lengths where candidate witness signals deserve more weight.
Higher combined local triangle/C4 risk predicts a less desirable rewrite.
Larger k can be beneficial when local risk is below the fixed control threshold.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: proposals touching more sampled forbidden witnesses and higher-load removed edges, while creating fewer local short cycles and using more separated or remote reconnections, will reduce forbidden-cycle witnesses earlier than unstructured selection; the bounded selector-provenance bonus should provide only a small additional preference. This is falsifiable by comparing early accepted improvement against an unstructured baseline.
assumptions: Larger sampled witness-touch counts predict greater forbidden-cycle reduction.
Larger removed-edge witness loads and concentration predict greater reduction.
Greater separation among removed edges is beneficial.
More remote newly connected endpoints are beneficial.
Higher local triangle and C4 risk predicts worse rewrites.
Selector provenance tags have a weak directional association with proposal quality, but are not ground truth.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: weighting sampled witness coverage by current capped load, then favoring separated removals and remote reconnections while penalizing local cycle risk, will select mutations that reduce forbidden-cycle witnesses more reliably than unstructured selection, especially when witness evidence is tied.
assumptions: Breaking more sampled witnesses predicts greater forbidden-cycle reduction.
Higher current capped witness counts identify more valuable lengths to target.
Greater mean distance between removed edges improves diversity of the rewrite.
Greater minimum preexisting distance for new edges makes reconnection more beneficial.
Higher combined local triangle and C4 risk predicts a less favorable rewrite.

seeds.design_summary: Hypothesis: Compared with unstructured selection, favoring proposals that touch more sampled forbidden-cycle witnesses while penalizing local triangle and 4-cycle creation will reduce authoritative forbidden-witness penalty earlier in bounded trajectories; this is falsified if these rankings systematically perform no better or worse than unstructured selection.
assumptions: A larger aggregate count of broken sampled witnesses predicts greater reduction of forbidden-cycle witnesses after rewriting.
The sum across configured lengths is a useful aggregate despite differing cycle lengths and sampling budgets.
A larger local triangle risk predicts more harmful newly created structure and should reduce priority.
A larger local 4-cycle risk predicts more harmful newly created structure and should reduce priority.
Capping each signal at 16 preserves useful ordering while limiting outlier influence, and the 8:1:1 weighting makes sampled witness breakage the principal signal.
